1. Access & Identity Management!access_i.aim_comments: The organization restricts access to cardholder data by business need to know through role-based access control (RBAC), least privilege, and separation of duties principles as described in the retrieved context.
The organization identifies and authenticates access through an internal password policy, mandatory MFA for production systems, centralized SSO usage, and role-based access control (RBAC) principles.

The production network is segmented into different zones based on security levels. The 'ClientABC' Clusters are deployed in a dedicated virtual environment (VPC for AWS/GCP or VNet for Azure) that fully isolates data and prevents inbound internet access, utilizing security groups as virtual firewalls.

The business stores and processes cardholder data in production systems using AES-256 encryption at rest and TLS 1.2 or higher for data in transit. Data is transmitted only within the production environment and never leaves it. Third-party vendors are used for processing, and they contractually comply with security standards. Sensitive data is also kept in hard copy (paper) for specific assets like contracts and forms.

Row [id=23.1] explicitly confirms the use of cryptographic frameworks (TLS 1.2) to secure data in transit over public networks. Row [id=22.7] further supports this by stating that all network traffic over public networks is sent over cryptographically sound encrypted connections.

2. Network & Infrastructure!network_infr.net_evidence: id=18.1 states that the production environment is subject to an external penetration test by a nationally recognized security firm at least once per calendar year.
[id=20.2] states that all 'ClientABC' managed workstations run up to date anti-virus and anti-malware software, and BYOD devices comply with the company's policy.

The vendor confirms they have formally defined criteria for notifying clients during incidents impacting data or system security. Specifically, 'ClientABC' will notify the client without undue delay upon becoming aware of any Data Breach. The notification includes a description of the nature and cause of the breach, expected resolution time, and subsequent updates on root cause evaluation, impact, remediation actions, and prevention plans.
[id=27.1] confirms the existence of a Security Incident Response Program with procedures and timeframes for notifying affected customers.
